subject: Onboarding Benchmark Ops Blueprint & Telemetry Handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@bluefolio.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmarking scope for Redwood onboarding

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. BlueFolio is ready to move into the onboarding benchmark phase and we want to confirm scope and targets before we book test windows with infra. High-level asks:

- Baseline latency (p95) and throughput targets for our production prompt mix
- Load-test plan (ramp, steady state, concurrency) and run duration
- Telemetry and artifacts you will share after runs (CSV exports / traces / GPU telemetry)

Can you propose an ops blueprint and a short checklist of artifacts we should expect for acceptance? We have a tentative test week of Sep 13–17 (US business hours).

Jordan
Ops Lead, BlueFolio

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@bluefolio.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking scope for Redwood onboarding

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've sketched an "Onboarding Benchmark Ops Blueprint" and attached a working spreadsheet (benchplan-v0.1.xlsx) with the proposed targets and the test matrix. Summary below — please review and flag anything we should adjust before we lock test windows.

Recommended acceptance targets (initial):
- Latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms (end-to-end generation for your 512-token average prompt)
- Throughput: steady-state 110–130 requests/sec (depends on batching; plan assumes 8-token avg generation per request)
- Tail safety: 99th percentile token latency < 900ms
- Error budget: < 1% 5xxs during steady state

Proposed load-test plan:
- Warmup: gradual ramp 0 -> 40 concurrent workers over 8 minutes (cache warmup included)
- Steady runs: three separate steady-state runs, each 30 minutes at 110 rps, with a 10-minute cool-down between runs
- Spike test: 5-minute burst to 180 rps to validate graceful degradation/fallbacks

Telemetry & artifacts we'll provide after each run:
- Per-request CSV (p50/p95/p99 latencies, status codes)
- GPU utilization traces (1s resolution), CPU and memory summaries
- Token/sec and aggregate token counts per run
- KV cache hit rates and effective throughput
- Load test script (jmeter) and command line used

Next steps / asks for BlueFolio:
- Confirm test window (we tentatively reserved Sep 14, 15 mornings PT)
- Provide canonical prompt set and representative payload sizes (JSON lines or compressed archive)
- Confirm whether you want privacy-preserving sampling or full texts for tokens export

I've cc'd Monica and Ben to capture run orchestration and test harness details. Attaching: benchplan-v0.1.xlsx (workbook), we'll iterate.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the sheet.

— Aisha
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@bluefolio.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking scope for Redwood onboarding

Jordan / team —

A few operational clarifications from infra/runtime side to make the runs reproducible:

- KV cache warmup: plan to replay a 15% prefix set at low concurrency for 10m before the main warmup to populate the KV cache. Otherwise first-run p95 will be noisy.
- Batching: We will use adaptive batching with a 20ms max batch delay. Our steady-state targets assume average batch size ~3–4 sequences. If you have strict per-request timing we can force smaller batches (cost trade-off).
- Warmup & steady ordering: do Warmup -> Steady 1 -> Cooldown -> Steady 2 -> Cooldown -> Steady 3 -> Spike -> Tear-down.

Load test commands (example):
- jmeter -n -t loadscript-jmeter.jmx -JtargetRPS=110 -Jduration=1800 -Jconcurrency=40 -l run1.jtl
- We'll convert JTL to summary CSV and attach.

Metrics we'll collect (and ingest to shared Drive):
- request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), http_status, token_count, tokens_per_sec
- gpu_util_pct, cpu_user_pct, system_load, mem_free_mb
- cache_hit_ratio

I'll attach the jmeter script (loadscript-jmeter.jmx) and a small helper to convert JTL->CSV. We'll also log the exact model pin/version and quantization profile used for each run.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@bluefolio.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking scope for Redwood onboarding

Thanks — adding a quick delivery checklist so we have parity on acceptance artifacts. Please treat this as the minimum evidence bundle we will hand over after each steady-state run:

1) run-summary-<date>.csv (per-request rows, anonymized prompt_id, latency_ms, status)
2) telemetry-gpu-<date>.csv (1s resolution)
3) tokens-summary-<date>.json (counts and token/sec profile)
4) run-flamegraph-<date>.svg (if available)
5) run-config.txt (jmeter args, model pin, quantization, routing policy)
6) checklist.pdf (signed off by BlueFolio engineering)

I've attached the evidence-template.csv to show the column layout we expect. For drive location, please upload to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cBenchOps and post the link.

Note on privacy: if BlueFolio prefers privacy-preserving outputs, we can provide prompt hashes and non-reversible tokens summary instead of raw prompts. Let us know preference before test week.

Priya
Customer Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@bluefolio.com>

Team —

This looks great and very thorough. Confirmation: we prefer anonymized prompts (hashes) for telemetry export. Sept 14 morning PT works for our first steady-state run; please reserve Sep 14 09:00–12:00 PT.

Two quick asks:
- Can you include a short canary policy for the spike test (rollback thresholds for error rate / p95)?
- Will Redwood provide a single service account key for the drive upload, or do we create the folder and invite your team?

If you can confirm those two items we'll mark this as green on our side and update the internal ops calendar. Thank you all for the quick turnaround.

Jordan
Ops Lead, BlueFolio
